title: Optional portable Cause model
summary: Normative binary Cause algebra for typed failure, portable defect, interruption, and semantic composition.

result_compatibility: Result<T,E> and Err<E> remain unchanged and accept every previously valid E
Cause<E> is separate and opt-in; no Result operation implicitly constructs or unwraps Cause
Arbitrary E is preserved in Fail and becomes portable only through a caller-selected explicit codec

variants.semantics: Absence of a cause; it is a valid Cause value.
Expected typed failure carrying exactly one E value.
Unexpected defect represented by a portable structured Failure, never a runtime exception object.
Interruption represented by a portable structured Failure, never a runtime fiber, thread, or process identity.
Ordered binary composition: left occurred before right; grouping is significant and preserved.
Binary concurrent composition; grouping is significant and child order is preserved for deterministic transport.

topology_policy: The variant set is exactly Empty, Fail, Die, Interrupt, Sequential, and Parallel
Sequential and Parallel are binary nodes and MUST NOT be flattened, reordered, deduplicated, or re-associated by a lossless codec
Cycles are forbidden in source object graphs and portable representations
Failure.causes is diagnostic ancestry only and MUST NOT encode, reconstruct, or substitute for Cause topology
codec_policy: A portable Cause codec MUST receive an explicit codec for E; no universal serialization of arbitrary E is implied
Encoding and decoding MUST preserve each tag, binary grouping, child order, and every codec-preserved E value
A decoder MUST reject unknown tags, unknown fields, unsupported Failure versions, cycles, and resource-limit violations
